qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant regional banking franchise in the Canton of Vaud supported by cantonal majority ownership (67%) and an explicit cantonal guarantee on retail deposits, creating a highly sticky, low-cost deposit base and ~30%+ local market share. Pricing power demonstrated by resilient net interest margins through interest rate cycles and consistent 11.0-12.5% ROE.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Banque Cantonale Vaudoise operates as a regional cantonal bank legally restricted to the Canton of Vaud, capping geographic expansion runway in a mature, saturated economy. In accordance with the Mauboussin persistence framework, commercial fractional-reserve banking sits in Tier 4 with rapid return fade (high fade rate f=0.29-0.30). Furthermore, net interest margins face terminal margin pressure from digital banking alternatives and Swiss National Bank rate cycle compression, limiting competitive advantage longevity below the required 15-year hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle ROE has averaged 11.0-12.5% (12.5% in 2023, 11.5% in 2024, 11.0% in 2025) with a steady cost-to-income ratio of 53-56%. While BCVN possesses strong local solvency (CET1 >18%) and low historical credit loss provisions, its statutory public mandate binds operations to Canton de Vaud, eliminating external reinvestment runways. Fractional-reserve asset base (>CHF 55B on ~CHF 4B equity) exposes earnings power to central bank rate regimes and commoditized mortgage competition.
